_doc: Authentication and authorization guidance per scan rule, read by _auth.py. area: authn (who are you), authz (what may you do), secrets (keys and credentials the auth depends on), session. today: what the code does now, in plain words. core: the ASP.NET Core way. aws: AWS options, the first one recommended. Wording only: detection stays in rules.json.

AUTH-WINDOWS.label: Windows authentication (IIS)
AUTH-WINDOWS.today: IIS signs users in with their Windows / Active Directory account (Kerberos / NTLM).
AUTH-WINDOWS.core: Negotiate authentication (Microsoft.AspNetCore.Authentication.Negotiate) works on Linux only with a keytab and a domain-joined service account; OpenID Connect to the client's IdP is simpler.
aws: OpenID Connect to the client's IdP (Entra ID / AD FS), or Amazon Cognito federated with it; the ALB can do the OIDC sign-in
AWS Managed Microsoft AD or AD Connector + Negotiate with a keytab (Linux)
Stay on Windows (EC2 / Windows containers) joined to the domain

AUTH-IMPERSONATION.label: Impersonation / Windows identity in code
AUTH-IMPERSONATION.today: Code runs as, or reads, the signed-in Windows user (WindowsIdentity, impersonate=true).
AUTH-IMPERSONATION.core: No impersonation on Linux: pass the user as claims, give the service its own identity.
aws: IAM role for the task (ECS task role) for AWS access; service accounts in Secrets Manager for other systems
Stay on Windows if a downstream system needs the user's own Windows identity

AUTH-FORMS-MEMBERSHIP.label: Forms authentication / Membership
AUTH-FORMS-MEMBERSHIP.today: Forms auth cookie with users and roles from the ASP.NET Membership / Role provider tables.
AUTH-FORMS-MEMBERSHIP.core: ASP.NET Core cookie authentication + ASP.NET Core Identity (rehash passwords at next sign-in).
aws: Amazon Cognito user pool with a user migration Lambda trigger (users move at first sign-in, no reset)
ASP.NET Core Identity on Amazon RDS / Aurora (users stay in the app database)

AUTH-CUSTOM-LOGIN.label: Custom login page, user kept in session
AUTH-CUSTOM-LOGIN.today: A hand-made login page puts the user object in session; pages check the session and redirect to the login page.
AUTH-CUSTOM-LOGIN.core: Cookie authentication + [Authorize] (or a fallback policy); the login page signs in with HttpContext.SignInAsync.
aws: Amazon Cognito user pool (hosted sign-in or ALB OIDC authentication) when users can move
Keep the local login with ASP.NET Core cookie auth; session (if still needed) on Amazon ElastiCache

AUTH-DB-CREDENTIAL-CHECK.label: Credentials checked against the app's own database
AUTH-DB-CREDENTIAL-CHECK.today: User name and password are checked by the application's own code or stored procedure against its user table.
AUTH-DB-CREDENTIAL-CHECK.core: An ASP.NET Core authentication handler wraps the existing check (one place, tested).
aws: Amazon Cognito with a user migration Lambda trigger that calls the existing check once per user
Keep the database check; the database moves to Amazon RDS with the app

AUTH-REVERSIBLE-PASSWORD.label: Passwords encrypted, not hashed
AUTH-REVERSIBLE-PASSWORD.today: Passwords are stored encrypted and can be decrypted with a key the application holds.
AUTH-REVERSIBLE-PASSWORD.core: ASP.NET Core Identity PasswordHasher (PBKDF2), rehash at next sign-in.
aws: Amazon Cognito (passwords never in the app)
Interim: the encryption key in AWS KMS / Secrets Manager, never in config

AUTH-FIXED-HEADER-SECRET.label: Fixed header value written in the code
AUTH-FIXED-HEADER-SECRET.today: A request is trusted when a header equals a value that is written in the source code.
AUTH-FIXED-HEADER-SECRET.core: An authentication handler that compares against a secret from configuration (Secrets Manager), per client.
aws: Amazon Cognito app clients (OAuth 2.0 client credentials) per calling app
Amazon API Gateway API keys with usage plans
At minimum: the value in AWS Secrets Manager, rotated

AUTH-API-KEY.label: API keys
AUTH-API-KEY.today: Clients send a shared API key in a header; the application checks it.
AUTH-API-KEY.core: An authentication handler with keys from configuration.
aws: Amazon API Gateway API keys + usage plans (throttling per client) in front of the service
Keys in AWS Secrets Manager read by the handler

AUTH-IP-CHECK.label: Client IP checks
AUTH-IP-CHECK.today: Code reads the caller's IP address (allow-lists, rate limits or logging).
AUTH-IP-CHECK.core: UseForwardedHeaders with the load balancer as a known proxy, so the real client IP is used.
aws: AWS WAF IP sets on the ALB / API Gateway for allow-lists
Security groups / NACLs for network-level allow-lists

AUTH-CONFIG-RULES.label: web.config <authorization> rules
AUTH-CONFIG-RULES.today: Folders and pages are protected by <allow> / <deny> rules in web.config.
AUTH-CONFIG-RULES.core: Authorization policies ([Authorize(Policy)], fallback policy, endpoint conventions); web.config rules are ignored.
aws: No AWS service: rewrite as policies and test every protected URL

AUTH-ROLES-CODE.label: Role checks
AUTH-ROLES-CODE.today: Code checks the user's role (IsInRole, [Authorize(Roles)], PrincipalPermission).
AUTH-ROLES-CODE.core: Claims-based policies; the new identity provider must issue the same roles.
aws: Amazon Cognito groups mapped to role claims
IdP group claims (Entra ID / AD FS)

AUTH-CUSTOM-AUTHZ-CODE.label: Hand-written access checks
AUTH-CUSTOM-AUTHZ-CODE.today: The application decides who may call what in its own methods (Authorize...()).
AUTH-CUSTOM-AUTHZ-CODE.core: An IAuthorizationHandler or middleware that runs on every request; tests per rule.
aws: Amazon Verified Permissions if the rules grow into a policy model; otherwise keep them in code

AUTH-JWT.label: JSON Web Tokens
AUTH-JWT.today: The application issues or validates JWTs.
AUTH-JWT.core: AddJwtBearer for validation; signing keys from KMS / Secrets Manager.
aws: Amazon Cognito as the issuer; API Gateway JWT authorizer
Signing keys in AWS KMS

AUTH-OWIN-OAUTH.label: OWIN OAuth server / cookies
AUTH-OWIN-OAUTH.today: The app is its own OAuth server or uses OWIN cookie middleware.
AUTH-OWIN-OAUTH.core: No built-in OAuth server: OpenIddict or Duende IdentityServer, or an external issuer.
aws: Amazon Cognito as the OAuth 2.0 / OIDC issuer
OpenIddict in the app (keys in KMS)

AUTH-BASIC.label: HTTP Basic authentication
AUTH-BASIC.today: User name and password in every request header (inbound or outbound).
AUTH-BASIC.core: An authentication handler (inbound); credentials from configuration (outbound).
aws: Amazon Cognito client credentials for machine clients
AWS Secrets Manager for outbound credentials

AUTH-WSFED.label: WS-Federation / AD FS
AUTH-WSFED.today: Sign-in is delegated to AD FS over WS-Federation (WIF).
AUTH-WSFED.core: Microsoft.AspNetCore.Authentication.WsFederation, or OpenID Connect to the same AD FS.
aws: Keep AD FS / Entra ID; register the new AWS URLs
Amazon Cognito federated with AD FS (SAML)

AUTH-IDENTITY2.label: ASP.NET Identity 2 (OWIN)
AUTH-IDENTITY2.today: ASP.NET Identity 2 user store and OWIN cookies.
AUTH-IDENTITY2.core: ASP.NET Core Identity (schema migration; password hashes are compatible).
aws: ASP.NET Core Identity on Amazon RDS / Aurora
Amazon Cognito with a user migration trigger

AUTH-EXTERNAL-IDP.label: External identity provider (OIDC)
AUTH-EXTERNAL-IDP.today: Sign-in already goes to an external OpenID Connect provider.
aws: Keep the IdP; add the AWS redirect URIs; client secret in Secrets Manager
ALB OIDC authentication in front of the app

AUTH-ASPNETCORE.label: ASP.NET Core authentication
AUTH-ASPNETCORE.today: Already uses the ASP.NET Core authentication pipeline.
aws: Secrets in AWS Secrets Manager; Amazon Cognito if the provider changes

AUTH-MACHINEKEY.label: machineKey
AUTH-MACHINEKEY.today: Cookies, view state and tokens are protected with a machineKey shared by the servers.
AUTH-MACHINEKEY.core: ASP.NET Core Data Protection with a shared key ring.
aws: Data Protection keys in Amazon S3 encrypted with AWS KMS (or ElastiCache / Parameter Store)

AUTH-DEFAULT-CREDENTIALS.label: Outbound calls as the Windows service account
AUTH-DEFAULT-CREDENTIALS.today: Outbound HTTP / SQL calls use the process's Windows account (DefaultCredentials).
aws: AWS Secrets Manager credentials; IAM roles for AWS services

DATA-INTEGRATED-SECURITY.label: Windows-integrated database login
DATA-INTEGRATED-SECURITY.today: The database connection signs in as the Windows service account.
DATA-INTEGRATED-SECURITY.core: SQL login (or Kerberos with a keytab on Linux).
aws: SQL authentication with the password in AWS Secrets Manager (rotation)
IAM database authentication (Aurora PostgreSQL / MySQL)

WEB-AMBIENT-PRINCIPAL.label: Ambient current user
WEB-AMBIENT-PRINCIPAL.today: Code reads the user from Thread.CurrentPrincipal / ClaimsPrincipal.Current.
WEB-AMBIENT-PRINCIPAL.core: IHttpContextAccessor or an ICurrentUser service injected where needed.
aws: No AWS service: code change in the port

IIS-SESSION-STATE.label: Session state
IIS-SESSION-STATE.today: Session state is kept in process or in a session server.
aws: Amazon ElastiCache (Valkey / Redis)
Amazon DynamoDB

STATE-SESSION.label: Session use in code
STATE-SESSION.today: Code stores per-user data in session.
aws: Amazon ElastiCache (Valkey / Redis)

user-facing.title: People sign in (web UI)
user-facing.aws: Amazon Cognito user pool (users migrated with a Lambda trigger at first sign-in), sign-in at the ALB (OIDC) or in the app; federate with the client's IdP if staff use it
user-facing.core: Cookie authentication + [Authorize] with a fallback policy; roles as claims
user-facing.why: One identity store with MFA, password policy and lockout handled by AWS; the app stops storing passwords.

windows.title: Staff sign in with Windows accounts
windows.aws: OpenID Connect to the client's IdP (Entra ID / AD FS) at the ALB or in the app; AWS Managed Microsoft AD + keytab only if Windows auth must stay
windows.why: Kerberos on Linux containers needs keytabs and domain trust; OIDC removes the domain dependency.

machine.title: Other systems call the API
machine.aws: Amazon API Gateway (or ALB) in front with AWS WAF; per-client credentials from Amazon Cognito (OAuth 2.0 client credentials) or API Gateway API keys; existing message-level checks kept in an ASP.NET Core authentication handler
machine.core: Authentication handler + authorization policies; secrets from AWS Secrets Manager
machine.why: Bad callers are stopped before the container; credentials are per client and rotatable.

existing-idp.title: Already uses an identity provider
existing-idp.aws: Keep the provider; register the AWS URLs; secrets in AWS Secrets Manager

none.title: No authentication found in code
none.aws: Confirm what protects it today (network, IIS settings, a gateway); on AWS put it in private subnets behind an internal ALB with security groups
none.why: Code shows no sign-in or access check: protection is outside the app, or missing.
